question.text: An air bubble of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> rises from the bottom of a lake <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> deep to the surface at a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The atmospheric pressure is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the density of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo><mo> </mo></math>There is no difference of the temperature of water at the depth of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and on the surface. The volume of air bubble when it reaches the surface will be

solution.text:
The pressure at the bottom of the lake can be calculated as follows:

Pbottom= P0 + ρgh=105+1000 × 10 × 40 Pa=5×105 Pa 

As the temperature of water remains constant, it can be written that

PbottomVbottom=PtopVtop   ...(1)

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface.

5×105×1=1×105×Vtop⇒Vtop=5×105×11×105 cm3= 5 cm3
